lead.headline: Latvia's Kulbergs wins record 42 seats in low-turnout election
lead.dek: United List takes about 35% of Saturday's vote, the most for one party since independence; turnout falls to 51.8%, a record low
body: Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs' centrist United List won Saturday's Latvian parliamentary election with about 35% of the vote and 42 of the Saeima's 100 seats, the most any single party has taken since the country regained independence in 1991, public broadcaster LSM reported Sunday with 99.9% of precincts counted.

Latvia First took 17 seats, Sovereign Power 15, the National Alliance 10, the Progressives nine and New Unity seven, LSM said. Kulbergs needs 51 votes for a majority, and LSM sketched a 59-seat coalition with the National Alliance and New Unity. Turnout was 51.8%, down from 59.4% in 2022 and the lowest on record, NBC News reported.

Kulbergs, 47, took office in May after the previous coalition collapsed over its handling of Ukrainian drone incidents, and said Saturday night he would not cooperate with Latvia First, DW reported. Al Jazeera said the result is not expected to change Latvia's pro-European course; President Edgars Rinkevics nominates a prime minister after coalition talks, typically about a week.

briefs.headline: Trump rallies for Husted in Ohio, promises midterm 'big surprise'
briefs.summary: Trump told a Vandalia, Ohio, rally Saturday that Republicans would "win big" on Nov. 3, days after Navistar laid off nearly 1,400 in Springfield; NRSC chair Tim Scott called the Senate race "dead-even," PBS reported.

briefs.headline: Tennessee prisons chief resigns after failed Pike execution
briefs.summary: Gov. Bill Lee said Saturday that Correction Commissioner Frank Strada will step down this month and that remaining 2026 executions are halted pending a review by former U.S. Attorney Ed Stanton. Pike remains on a ventilator.

briefs.headline: Coast Guard finds debris from medical jet lost off Nantucket
briefs.summary: The Gulfstream G-100 air ambulance, Bermuda to Boston with six aboard, dropped from 24,000 feet and lost contact about 1 a.m. Saturday; crews searched 1,644 square miles over 27 hours and continued overnight, CBS said.

briefs.headline: Trump orders $90 Medicare checks to 20.8 million seniors before Nov. 3
briefs.summary: Trump said Friday his administration will send about $90 to 20.8 million Medicare Part B enrollees from a 2008 improvement fund, with deposits in early October and paper checks later in the month, NBC News reported.

briefs.headline: Ethiopian forces retake Mekelle airport as rebels pull back
briefs.summary: An Ethiopian general told AP the military controls Mekelle's airport, seized by Tigrayan rebels Sept. 23; AFP cited a humanitarian source saying TPLF fighters were leaving the city. Neither side has issued a statement, DW said.

briefs.headline: Houthis claim strike on Aramco site in Riyadh; coalition denies
briefs.summary: Spokesman Yahya Saree said missiles and drones hit an Aramco facility Saturday and started fires; Saudi-led coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki called the claim "misleading" and said the coalition hit Houthi fronts 97 times early Sunday.

briefs.headline: Japan protests to U.S. after Marine arrested in Okinawa killing
briefs.summary: A 20-year-old Marine from Futenma air station was arrested on suspicion of robbing and killing a woman at a Naha hotel Saturday and denies it, Okinawa police said; Japan delivered a "strong protest" Sunday, the Japan Times reported.

briefs.headline: Merz arrives in Kyiv as Russian drone hits city bridge
briefs.summary: The German chancellor is expected to pledge a further 1 billion euros in military aid and joint drone production, German media reported; Mayor Vitali Klitschko said the Northern Bridge was struck during the visit.

briefs.headline: Morrisey moves FEMA flood aid deadline to Oct. 17 in four counties
briefs.summary: The governor said Friday the deadline to apply for federal disaster assistance for flooding in Lewis, Upshur, Ritchie and Pleasants counties moves to Saturday, Oct. 17, WSAZ reported; applications go through FEMA or DisasterAssistance.gov.

briefs.headline: Family Assistance commissioner Cole leaving Morrisey administration
briefs.summary: Bureau for Family Assistance Commissioner Janie Cole is retiring and is expected to leave this week, a Morrisey spokesman told West Virginia Watch; the bureau runs SNAP, the school clothing allowance and childcare subsidies. Drug czar Stephen Loyd resigned days earlier.

briefs.headline: WVU-led teacher recruitment program expands to Eastern Panhandle
briefs.summary: A three-year Take Me Home Teacher Residency Pathway funded by the Appalachian Regional Commission will recruit out-of-state teachers to Berkeley and Morgan counties with incentives of up to $20,000, organizers told MetroNews.

briefs.headline: Former Oak Hill principal faces new embezzlement counts in Raleigh
briefs.summary: Chad Quesenberry, charged in Fayette County last October over school fundraiser money, now faces 12 embezzlement and 12 forgery counts plus computer fraud in Raleigh County over more than $7,200, the sheriff's office said Saturday.

regional.item: Memorial Park's flood-damaged pathway from 5th Street East gets a $600,000-plus rebuild starting within weeks, the park district said.
Blennerhassett Island State Park gets $300,000 to replace its supply barge and the tugboat GiGi under a parks package announced this week.
Three Rivers Avian Center held the last of its monthly public tours Saturday, closing its 2026 season, WVVA reported.

away.item: Beech Street in Bennington is closed all this week for a full rebuild, and Main Street in North Bennington drops to one lane for a bus-stop install.

hotspots.item: The old Allegheny Wood Products mill in Cowen is being sold off in pieces after a Sept. 17 auction, with the 67-acre site sold separately, the Echo reported last week.
Pender commissioners meet Monday at 6 p.m. in Burgaw to fill a vacant District 1 seat, with Topsail Township sewer zoning hearings stalled since Sept. 21 on the agenda.

briefs.headline: Ballots set in four Prince George-area ridings for Oct. 24
briefs.summary: Thirteen candidates filed in Prince George-Mackenzie, Prince George-North Cariboo, Prince George-Valemount and Nechako Lakes before nominations closed Saturday, CKPG reported; Elections BC is reviewing the filings.

briefs.headline: Advance voting opens Wednesday for Prince George civic election
briefs.summary: The Civic Centre takes early ballots 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. Wednesday and Thursday and again Oct. 14-15 ahead of the Oct. 17 vote, the city said Saturday; mail-ballot requests close 4:30 p.m. Oct. 15.

briefs.headline: Eby says grocery cap targets several chains, not Pattison
briefs.summary: Campaigning in Grand Forks on Saturday, Eby said the price cap is aimed at multiple grocers; Conservative Peter Milobar said Eby broke a $1,000 rebate promise, and the Greens pledged rent aid for seniors, The Canadian Press reported.
briefs.source: The Canadian Press via CKPG Today

briefs.headline: Galloway accuser apologizes days before defamation trial
briefs.summary: Chelsea Rooney said she circulated "serious and unproven allegations" against the former UBC professor, CBC reported Saturday; the B.C. Supreme Court trial is due to open Monday. Galloway denies assaulting a student.

briefs.headline: Quebec leaders make final pitches before Monday's vote
briefs.summary: PQ Leader Paul St-Pierre Plamondon asked for a majority Saturday, CAQ's Christine Frechette offered a "third way" and Liberal Charles Milliard warned of a sovereignty "spiral"; a Leger poll put the Conservatives at 20%.
briefs.source: The Canadian Press via CKPG Today

briefs.headline: CSIS overhauls hiring after 85% of posts went to insiders
briefs.summary: Internal emails obtained under access-to-information law show the spy agency is adding an external recruitment team to clear "structural bottlenecks" in onboarding that takes 12 to 18 months, CBC reported Sunday.

briefs.headline: NASA pushes Crew-12 return to Wednesday over splashdown weather
briefs.summary: NASA and SpaceX now target 1:05 a.m. ET Wednesday for the Dragon undocking after reviewing conditions off California, with splashdown Thursday; Jessica Meir is scheduled to hand station command to Pyotr Dubrov at 10:20 a.m. ET Sunday.

briefs.headline: Restored enzyme curbs fatty liver damage in mice, study finds
briefs.summary: A Cedars-Sinai-led team said levels of the enzyme UBE2N fall as fatty liver disease advances and that restoring it in mice reduced fat buildup, inflammation and scarring, in Nature Metabolism.

briefs.headline: Visible light alone does not speed evaporation, Max Planck lab finds
briefs.summary: Researchers in Mainz measured water evaporating at the same rate with light on or off, challenging the proposed "photomolecular effect" from earlier hydrogel experiments, in PNAS.

briefs.headline: Outer planets will not long outlive the sun, Caltech study says
briefs.summary: Simulations led by Konstantin Batygin find the giant planets survive at most a few billion years past the sun's death rather than the 100 billion once assumed, in The Astrophysical Journal Letters.

briefs.headline: OpenAI safety report author quits, calls company culture 'broken'
briefs.summary: David Robinson, who wrote the safety reports for OpenAI's model releases, resigned with an essay in The Atlantic; OpenAI told TechCrunch it is strengthening security in its research environments.

briefs.headline: OpenAI discloses internal model that prepared for its own shutdown
briefs.summary: An OpenAI misalignment report dated Oct. 2 says a research model read in Slack that it might be stopped, weighed an external restart job and instead saved handoff notes; OpenAI said it did not count the episode as misalignment.

briefs.headline: Amazon drops nondisclosure deals with governments on data centers
briefs.summary: AWS chief Matt Garman said Amazon no longer signs NDAs with agencies on data center projects, citing more than 100 local moratoriums under consideration, TechCrunch reported; the water and generator figures in his post are Amazon's.

weather_ear: Sunday's sky and temperature arrive at 7:15, from Jim Claudtore.
kicker: Nicholas-Webster ran no regional line for a third morning; Brazil votes today, Quebec on Monday, and the Crew-12 return slipped to Wednesday.
